risks: Emotional distress for women recalling a difficult birth and for staff recalling unsafe shifts; possible identification of staff in a small unit.
consent: Written informed consent after an information sheet in plain language and in the main local languages; consent reconfirmed before recording; participants may stop at any time.
data: Recordings transcribed and deleted; transcripts pseudonymised; staff roles described broadly in reports to avoid identification.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: women with limited English, from minority ethnic groups, with low income or young age may have the worst experiences of waiting and be least likely to volunteer. Recruitment through community midwives and the maternity voices group, interpreters and flexible interview times address this.
effectiveness: The study succeeds if the redesign group can link each recommendation to accounts from staff and women.
efficiency: Uses one protected day per week; no other costs.
costs: Interpreter bookings from the unit's existing budget.
grants: None needed; a regional midwifery research fellowship could support a later evaluation of the redesign.
partnerships: Maternity voices partnership, community midwifery team, antenatal clinic manager, bed management team.
rebPath: Full research ethics committee review is required because women are interviewed about a potentially distressing experience; the application has not been submitted yet and no recruitment starts before approval.
limitations: One unit; insider researcher; women's accounts are retrospective.
summary: Interviews need full ethics review, not yet submitted; distress protocol and equity-focused recruitment.
